Title: When bin packing meets facility location: A case study of unmanned aerial vehicle charging-station location and task assignment for insulator cleaning
The Time-Aware Probabilistic Kraljic Matrix: From supplier segmentation to SaaS customer retention
Authors: Renata Pelissari, Letícia Nunes Camillo, Maria Célia de Oliveira, Betania Silva Carneiro Campello
Abstract: Customer segmentation is an important competitive strategy for organizations, as it allows them to identify distinct groups of customers with different needs and values, enabling a smarter allocation of resources. This study introduces a novel methodology for customer segmentation which can be seen as a probabilistic extension of the Kraljic matrix. The proposal utilizes the SMAA–FFS–H method to incorporate a hierarchical criteria structure within the Kraljic matrix dimensions named Profit Impact and Supply Risk. The probabilistic approach allows for dealing with uncertainties and provides a probability distribution for each supplier’s classification. In addition, we adapt the probabilistic Kraljic approach to SaaS customer classification and retention, replacing the original dimensions by Revenue Impact and Churn Risk and incorporating time-series descriptors of Customer Success indicators. A case study with SaaS clients illustrates the managerial insights for proactive retention strategies.

Title: Compete or co-operate: Revenue sharing and copyright disputes for long-form and short-form video platforms
Authors: Jing Li, Yulin Zhang, Xianyu Yu, Xin Zhang, Mark Goh

Title: Dynamic pricing and adoption of electric vehicles under critical mineral resource constraints
Authors: Hongtao Ren, Zanfeng Wang, Xiao-Bing Zhang, Wenji Zhou

Title: How return policies impact the brand owner’s AI adoption strategy
Authors: Jing Lyu, Yanju Zhou, Ming Chen
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in online retail to reduce product fit uncertainty. This paper develops a game-theoretic model with consumer learning to investigate how platform return policies shape AI adoption and market outcomes. The model assumes that a brand owner sells through an e-commerce platform. The analysis examines the brand owner's pricing and AI adoption decisions under no-return and lenient return policies. It allows for three types of AI adoption strategies: no AI, platform-provided AI, and jointly developed AI. The results show that return policies alter the economic value of AI-generated information, thereby shaping the brand owner's pricing and AI adoption decisions. Under a no-return policy, the belief enhancement effect of AI can strengthen the brand owner's pricing power, while the profitability of AI adoption depends on the market fit rate. Under a lenient return policy, the screening effect of AI can reduce purchases by poorly matched consumers and the resulting return-processing losses. When the market fit rate is low, such screening can also reduce the attractiveness of a high-price strategy and lead to a lower equilibrium price. These differences reshape the brand owner's AI adoption incentives across return policy environments and alter the relative attractiveness of AI options with different effectiveness and implementation costs. Consequently, the distribution of benefits among market participants also varies across return-policy regimes. Under a no-return policy, AI adoption may be more favorable to the brand owner and the platform, whereas under a lenient return policy, it is more likely to generate a triple-win outcome for the brand owner, the platform, and consumers.

Title: Bidding strategies for energy storage operators in a 100% renewable electricity market: A game-theoretic approach
Authors: Arega Getaneh Abate, Dogan Keles, Xiufeng Liu, Salim Hassi, Xiao-Bing Zhang
Abstract: Large-scale energy storage is expected to be a pivotal source of flexibility in electricity systems supplied entirely by renewable energy sources (RES). However, its strategic role in market-based dispatch remains insufficiently understood. In a 100% RES market setting, storage can improve adequacy and renewable utilization by shifting energy across time. It can also acquire market power as the main flexible, price-making technology. In this paper, we develop a Cournot competition model in which storage operators choose quantity bids to maximize profit in a stylized day-ahead electricity market supplied only by RES. Market clearing is represented through residual-demand blocks so that renewable intermittency appears as an intertemporal arbitrage opportunity for storage operators. We formulate the storage operators’ problem in two tractable ways: (ii) a continuous reformulation based on demand blocks, and (ii) an equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model with big- M linearization. Nash equilibria are computed with an iterative best-response procedure and benchmarked against a centralized social planner problem to quantify efficiency losses from strategic behavior. The model is calibrated to Denmark’s DK1 bidding zone using 2024 day-ahead data and 2030 renewable-capacity and demand projections. The results show that storage reduces imbalances and improves welfare relative to a no-storage case. Concentrated ownership also creates incentives to withhold flexibility, raise prices, and slow the reduction of unmet demand and curtailment. These findings position storage as both a stabilizing resource and a potential source of market power, highlighting the importance of market designs that jointly consider competition, concentration, and capacity deployment in high-RES systems.

Title: From terroir to quality: Handling the run for efficiency across time and space for Italian agri-food firms
Abstract: In the actual increasingly competitive market for agricultural firms, the ability to turn inputs into outputs named efficiency has to be pursued by exploiting quality. We conceive quality as a game changer within the per se complex agriculture-environment link. We aim at exploring the critical junctures between efficiency, quality and territorial riskiness, considering space-sensitive products, whose quality is certified as linked to the terroir. We employ an integrated methodological approach of efficiency analysis, causal inference and machine learning. A conditional nonparametric efficiency estimator is assisted by the causal evaluation of the certification effects on efficiency over time, through difference-in-differences technique and genetic matching. Also, a machine learning technique called feature selection is used to make out-of-sample prediction of the efficiency score. The approach is applied to 1133 Italian agri-food firms, measured over 24 internal and external characteristics from 2015 to 2020. Italy stands for a best-practice in the quality products market, despite increasing territorial vulnerability. We question and later find that the collaboration – which is needed to sell certified products of origin – is a vital expedient to run for efficiency over time and by less-caring of spatial threats. Results are relevant for researchers, and promote some win-win strategies for governors and producers in a long-term oriented vision of the sector.

Title: Routing optimization for mixed fleet of single and multi-compartment vehicles considering oriented semi-hard arrival time consistency
Authors: Mahnaz Shoeib, Jafar Bagherinejad, Mahdi Bashiri
Abstract: Each perishable food must be stored at a specific temperature to ensure freshness and safety. Single compartment vehicles carry these incompatible products separately, while multi-compartment vehicles enable the joint delivery of these items. To meet customers’ demands over a multi-period planning horizon, a cost-effective combination of these vehicles should be used in a mixed fleet. Customers prefer consistent arrival times for deliveries during each period, which can improve service quality but may increase distribution costs. Therefore, the level of consistency should be carefully determined. This paper examines the oriented semi-hard consistency of arrival time in a multiperiod vehicle routing problem with split deliveries that arises in the distribution of incompatible products. The focus of this paper is on evaluating the effect of fleet type (single-compartment, multi-compartment, and mixed) on arrival time consistency. A mathematical model is presented to describe the problem of determining the consistency level along with the fleet type. Considering the NP-hardness of the problem, a matheuristic algorithm that includes fix-and-optimize and local search modules has been developed and compared against an adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm (ALNS). The developed mathematical model and solution algorithms have been tested and evaluated using numerical instances adopted from the literature. The experimental results indicate that the mixed fleet performs better than other fleets in terms of cost reduction and service consistency. Furthermore, the matheuristic algorithm outperforms the ALNS in terms of computational time and solution quality. The overall findings provide managerial insights for decision-makers involved in distributing various incompatible products.

Title: Sixty years of research on districting problems: Models, algorithms, and applications
Authors: Camilo Campos-Valdés, Eduardo Álvarez-Miranda, Jordi Pereira, Roger Z. Ríos-Mercado, Diana L. Huerta-Muñoz
Abstract: Districting consists of grouping small geographic areas or units into larger units, known as districts, territories, zones, or clusters, according to relevant planning criteria such as compactness, connectivity, and/or balance requirements, among others. This class of problems arises in many applications, such as political organization, sales territory design, school districting, commercial and distribution districting, service districting, and health care management, among others. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive state-of-the-art review of the districting literature over the last sixty years. First, a discussion of a general modeling structure is presented to identify the main components of the problem. Then, existing works are reviewed according to two distinct classifications: one by application area and another by modeling techniques and solution methodologies. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of the main challenges and future research lines in this exciting area of discrete optimization.

Title: Comparison of subsidy policies for mitigating workload imbalance in a two-tier service system
Authors: Yiling Ma, Peipei Wu, Xiaoli Wang, Xiaochuan Zhu

Title: A relax-and-fix and fix-and-optimize algorithm for physician scheduling in emergency rooms
Authors: Valdemar A.P.A. Devesse, Kerem Akartunalı, Marcio da S. Arantes, Claudio F.M. Toledo
Abstract: Balancing physician workload in emergency departments is a significant problem in practice due to its major impacts in a hospital setting, from severe cost implications to its effect on vital patients’ care. From a theoretical perspective, the problem involves simultaneously addressing several inherent and often conflicting challenges, such as ensuring a fair distribution of workload among physicians, respecting the availability of staff and minimizing costs in a rather expensive sector. In this paper, we propose a matheuristic to address this challenging problem. Based on a mixed-integer programming model from the literature, we first incorporate the modelling of least absolute deviation in a set of workload constraints. Our approach integrates relax-and-fix and fix-and-optimize heuristics that are effectively used in other domains such as production planning. We present detailed computational results that compare our approach with standard mixed-integer programming model using benchmark instances from the literature. Our approach has resulted in 1) a higher degree of satisfaction with demand requirements, 2) a more accurate estimation of working hours and a fairer distribution among physicians, and 3) shorter computational times to find feasible solutions.

Title: Equilibrium influence and pricing in duopoly competition
Authors: Reza Nazari Khanmiri, Xiao Huang, Georges Zaccour
Abstract: Competition for experience goods rarely hinges on price alone. When customers are uncertain about product fit, any attribute that shapes their posterior beliefs – brand reputation, online reviews, influencer endorsements, or money-back guarantees – becomes strategically significant. This study develops a duopoly model in which sellers compete through price and persuasion when consumers update beliefs via Bayesian persuasion and may return purchases. The equilibrium characterizes how sellers jointly craft price and influence decisions to gain competitive advantage. The seller with lower expected fit relies on influence to attract marginal consumers, while the higher-fit seller gains little from persuasion. Nonetheless, equilibrium dictates near-symmetric pricing, so competition plays out primarily through informational instruments rather than price undercutting. Influence can also reinforce rival loyalty by clarifying fit, revealing a double-edged strategic effect. Higher signal quality or tighter external price constraints compress loyal segments and increase the marginal value of persuasion. By modeling these interdependencies, the analysis clarifies how sellers can strategically align influence efforts, precision, and operational policies in competitive digital markets where consumer beliefs and transaction frictions jointly determine advantage.

Title: AI or human live sales? Live sales model selection and pricing strategies in a competitive market
Authors: Jianjian Chen, Wenfan Zhao, Lili Liu, Wei Yu, Sihua Chen
Abstract: In recent years, live sales have surged tremendously. Some retailers are increasingly hiring human streamers to reduce product uncertainty among consumers, while others, equipped with virtual streamers, are developing artificial intelligence (AI)-based live sales models to overcome problems such as weak streamer control and high live sales costs. This study develops a three-stage game model to investigate the live sales selection between AI and human live sales, as well as their pricing strategies in a competitive market. It elucidates how the live sales strategies vary with the network effect, market expansion effect, erosion effect, and consumer acceptance of AI live sales. Notably, as the scale of the consumer market softens retailer competition, a low or high degree of consumer acceptance of AI live sales can lead the retailer that adopts AI live sales to set a higher price. In a competitive live sales scenario, retailers should adopt AI live sales when the erosion effect is moderate and the network effect is weak, whereas human live sales become the equilibrium strategy when the erosion effect is weak or the network effect is strong; otherwise, competing retailers should adopt different live sales models. Finally, as consumer acceptance of AI live sales increases, the AA, HN, and NN strategies become more likely to be equilibrium strategies, while HA and HH are less likely to occur. Although the AN strategy initially becomes more likely to emerge as the equilibrium strategy, its likelihood ultimately decreases. The extension models confirm the robustness of the underlying conclusions.

Title: Timeliness-driven routing and scheduling for infrastructure rush repairs with cascading time uncertainties
Authors: Xinhao Cui, Penghao Qi, Bo Li, Yi Ren, Yiyong Xiao

Title: Competition and complementarity between online healthcare platform and offline hospital
Authors: Xi Yu, Jizhou Lu, Stephen Shum, Shenghao Zhang
Abstract: Motivated by the rapid expansion of online healthcare platforms, we study a healthcare system with online–offline interactions. We develop an analytical model capturing patient type uncertainty, service differentiation, heterogeneous cost structures of healthcare facilities, and patient flow across channels. This paper shows that the entry of third-party online healthcare platforms may create a diagnosis–treatment mismatch, even as they expand access to healthcare. Our study examines the competition and complementarity between online healthcare platforms and offline hospitals. We show that, under certain conditions, the online healthcare platform entry can increase the offline hospital's patient demand and profitability, leading to a win–win outcome. When the hospital's capacity cost pressure is moderate, the complementary effect dominates, improving both demand and profitability. When the hospital's capacity cost pressure is high, rising costs burden and diagnosis–treatment mismatch reduce both profitability and patient demand. When the hospital's capacity cost pressure is low, the competitive effect dominates, lowering profitability, while the impact on patient demand depends on whether cannibalization or price competition dominates. We further examine regulatory interventions aimed at addressing the diagnosis–treatment mismatch. However, we show that not all interventions can be useful in addressing this mismatch. While the price ceiling for the offline hospital does not incur any direct cost for the government, its application is limited. Compared with the service price subsidy, the capacity cost subsidy is more efficient in mitigating diagnosis–treatment mismatch. Improving online service quality can increase the overall treatment rate under moderate capacity cost pressure, but it does not resolve the mismatch when the offline hospital's capacity cost pressure is high. Overall, this study provides a unified framework for understanding the role of online healthcare platforms and offers managerial and policy insights for designing efficient healthcare systems with online–offline interactions.

Title: Integrating topic modeling and heuristic optimization for customer lifetime value in multi-channel decision support
Authors: Tzu-Chien Wang, Ruey-Shan Guo, Chialin Chen, Chia Kai Li
Abstract: As data-driven marketing evolves, firms face the challenge of translating predictive insights into strategic resource-allocation decisions. This study proposes a CLV decision-support architecture that integrates semantic representation, multi-stage behavioral prediction, and budget-constrained allocation. The architecture combines BERTopic-based semantic extraction and gradient boosting for predictive modeling with a finite-difference sensitivity-guided heuristic search module. Empirically, we separate observed temporal validation from semi-synthetic and simulation-based analyses. On the real temporal split, a predictive signal is present (AUC = 0.6313), but the integrated-versus-stage-wise uplift is small and not statistically significant. Controlled analyses instead show that integrated allocation becomes more visible under tighter budgets, stronger downstream coupling, and stress conditions. Within the BDE family, finite-difference guidance improves over vanilla BDE in the tested setting, but we retain this only as a narrow application-oriented claim. Overall, the findings support a bounded, condition-dependent view of semantic-aware CLV decision support rather than a claim of uniform deployment gains.

Title: Enhancing military load planning: A prioritized 2-D orthogonal packing approach
Authors: William K. Kirschenman, H. Sebastian Heese, Michael G. Kay, Russell E. King, Brandon M. McConnell
Abstract: Military combat loading requires arranging equipment on maritime transport vessels to enable rapid, prioritized off-loading while maintaining unit cohesion and vessel stability. Related maritime deck-loading settings can involve similar access, grouping, and balance requirements. This paper extends a prioritized two-dimensional orthogonal packing framework to incorporate global load balancing requirements alongside existing prioritization objectives. We study three solution approaches for this globally constrained problem: a monolithic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) approach, a sliding-window matheuristic, and a sliding-window matheuristic with in-stride load balancing penalties. For any sliding-window solution that fails to achieve both feasible packing and load balancing in the initial stage, we develop a universal post-processing strategy that selectively relaxes and re-optimizes item positions to achieve balance with minimal disruption to the prioritized layout. Computational experiments demonstrate that the matheuristic approaches fundamentally outperform the monolithic MILP approach in load balance reliability, solution quality, and computational efficiency, providing practical guidance for integrating automated optimization into military load planning systems. Among these, the simpler sliding-window matheuristic followed by post-processing repair emerges as the recommended practical configuration, offering the strongest overall combination of balance success, solution quality, and runtime, while the in-stride variant remains a narrower alternative when direct first-stage balance attainment is paramount. The matheuristic pipelines generate high-quality, load-balanced solutions for single-vessel scenarios within a few minutes on average, enabling rapid evaluation of multiple loading configurations during time-critical deployment planning.

Title: Editorial Board
Have inputs been substituted for each other? Nonparametric tests for factor substitution in banking data envelopment analysis
Abstract: ABSTRACT Standard Data Envelopment Analysis radial models such as CCR and BCC assume that inputs are substituted for each other along the efficiency frontier. However, this assumption is rarely verified empirically, creating the risk of specification bias if factors are not substituted. This paper introduces a nonparametric testing protocol to determine whether inputs have, in fact, been substituted for each other along the efficiency frontier. It employs Local Weighted Quantile Regression to estimate the partial derivatives of the input frontier directly from the data, classifying input pairs as substitutes or non-substitutes based on the sign and statistical significance of the estimated frontier slopes. The methodology is illustrated using Monte Carlo simulations of known substitute and non-substitute technologies. When applied to 2,534 U.S. commercial banks, the protocol finds no evidence of substitution for any input pair: 13 of 15 specifications classify the inputs as non-substitutes that increase and decrease together, and the remaining two yield positive but imprecisely estimated slopes. The paper then shows that applying the standard CCR model to the bank data results in substantial biases in bank efficiency scores. Finally, the paper identifies models that have been used to account for fixed proportion technologies.

Title: Programmatic or sponsored advertising? Control, costs, and consumer utility in platform competition
Authors: Dan Gao, He Xu, Stuart X. Zhu
Abstract: User-generated content platforms increasingly rely on advertising for monetization, with programmatic advertising (platform-controlled) and sponsored advertising (producer-controlled) representing two distinct formats. Sponsored advertising not only shifts decision rights from platforms to producers but also raises quality-related costs and alters consumer utility, which may be positive or negative. We develop a game-theoretic model to analyze competing producers’ advertising format choices. The equilibrium outcomes depend on three forces: the sponsorship-induced utility effect, the advertising effect, and the quality cost difference effect. When the sponsorship-induced utility effect is strongly negative, both producers adopt programmatic advertising, while a strongly positive effect leads both to adopt sponsored advertising. For moderate effects, equilibrium strategies hinge on advertising aversion: weak aversion favors asymmetric strategies, while stronger aversion reduces differentiation and may yield multiple symmetric equilibria. Increasing quality cost differences further discourages sponsored advertising. Our results reveal when platforms and producers benefit from delegating advertising control, and under what conditions sponsored advertising enhances platform profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. These findings contribute to the literature on digital platform operations and provide guidance for platforms in designing advertising models that balance monetization, content quality, and user experience.

Title: Auction design and operational strategy for hybrid recycling platforms under information asymmetry
Authors: Dongmei Xue, Ruud H. Teunter, Stuart X. Zhu, Weihua Zhou
Abstract: Online platforms for used products operate either as marketplaces that earn commission fees or as remanufacturers that purchase and refurbish items. An emerging hybrid structure integrates these roles, allowing platforms to capture both transaction-based and remanufacturing revenues. This paper develops an auction-based analytical model to examine how such a hybrid platform optimally designs its reservation price while internalizing dual revenue streams under product heterogeneity and information asymmetry. Within an independent private-value framework, the analysis shows that the optimal reservation price increases with the number of bidders—contrasting with classical auction predictions under limited competition. The results further characterize the conditions under which the platform optimally adopts a pure commission model, a pure remanufacturing model, or a hybrid structure, depending on its valuation and commission rate. By linking auction design to platform governance in reverse logistics markets, the study provides new insights into how digital intermediation shapes profitability and strategic configuration when managing heterogeneous used products.

Title: A hybrid cost efficiency model under fixed and non-fixed prices: A case study on the Polish justice courts
Authors: Magdalena Kapelko, Dimitrios Sotiros, Sebastian Klaudiusz Tomczak
Abstract: Measuring and improving public sector efficiency is key to delivering fair and effective services. As part of the public sector, justice courts, beyond handling legal matters, should pursue the efficient allocation of public resources. Therefore, their economic efficiency should be regularly assessed. However, studies evaluating the performance of justice courts rarely focus on the economic dimension of efficiency at the micro level. To fill this gap, the contribution of this study is twofold. Firstly, from the methodological point of view, relying on data envelopment analysis, we propose a new hybrid framework for measuring cost efficiency that is capable of handling exogenously fixed and non-fixed prices and allowing the latter to be endogenously optimized. Other advantages of the proposed framework include estimating realistic targets for non-fixed prices and utilized resources, exploring reallocation opportunities for resources, and identifying cost–demand relationships. Secondly, from the empirical perspective, we show the applicability of this new framework to Polish district courts over the period 2017–2021. The results reveal that only 10% of the courts are cost efficient. Interestingly, on average, the model suggests an increase in the number of all employees and in non-fixed salaries, as well as a reduction in the volume of capital. The results also suggest that the reallocation of resources can lead to significantly fewer pending cases or can eliminate them entirely. A further reduction in the number of pending cases can be potentially achieved by redistributing all registered cases under a centralized management system.

Title: Sustainable Steel Supply Chain Network Design under Export Taxes and Import Tariffs: A Multi-objective Stochastic Programming Framework
Authors: Navid Sahebjamnia, Vedat Verter, Amir Hossein Azadnia
Abstract: This paper introduces a two-stage stochastic programming model featuring multi-objective recourse functions to address the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability in steel supply chain networks. The model integrates strategic decisions (facility location, capacity acquisition, and technology selection) with tactical material flow coordination. The dynamics of steel industry-specific characteristics are captured through multi-scale time periods, technology compatibility requirements, and sustainability metrics based on location-technology-flow configurations. Furthermore, the model incorporates export taxes and import tariffs to optimise material flows between nationwide and global networks, enabling comprehensive analysis of how these policy tools influence strategic and tactical decisions whilst impacting sustainability objectives. A solution approach is developed using the ε-constraint and Sample Average Approximation methods to address demand uncertainty and the trade-offs among multiple recourse objectives. Novel algorithms are introduced to determine the upper and lower bounds of the constrained objective functions and to form the loops of the ε-constraint method. The model's application to a real-world case study demonstrates its effectiveness in achieving balanced material flows across the steel SCN after four strategic periods. Through sustainability assessment and analysis of various tax and tariff policies, we derive eight policy insights regarding their impacts on strategic and tactical decisions. The results confirm the model's capability to generate robust solutions that effectively balance network capacity against demand patterns while achieving sustainability objectives.

Title: When to offer refunds in probabilistic selling
Authors: Meng Wu, Yuetong Li, Tian Bai
Abstract: Probabilistic selling (PS) is an innovative selling approach that introduces uncertainty in product allocation, and has gained widespread popularity across various industries. PS leverages consumer risk stemming from uncertain product allocation to drive profit, with this risk serving as the cornerstone of its profit model, which is why refunds are typically not allowed. Motivated by the increasing adoption of full refund policies in probabilistic selling, this paper investigates how offering refunds influences the profitability of PS sales. Using a horizontally differentiated Hotelling model, we assess the profitability of three strategies: PS with no refund, PS with full refunds, and Deterministic Selling (DS), and determine the conditions under which each strategy is optimal. Our results indicate that while allowing returns might lower the proportion of consumers who purchase and ultimately keep probabilistic products, potentially reducing profits, it also attracts a larger customer base, thereby increasing overall sales and profitability. Therefore, when consumer preferences are less differentiated, offering a refund becomes the optimal strategy. Importantly, as probabilistic selling evolves from a PS+DS mix to a purely PS strategy, its comparative edge over DS weakens. Offering refunds can effectively reinforce the viability of PS.

Title: Mitigate undertreatment or not? Hospitals’ strategic operations in a two-tier healthcare system
Authors: Changhe Lai, Yanfei Lan, Ruiqing Zhao
Abstract: The prevalence of undertreatment worsens patients’ care experiences at the low-level community hospital and contributes to excessive demand for the high-level city hospital in a two-tier healthcare system. Undertreatment is generally attributed to the community hospital's incapacity to deliver timely and appropriate care. Hospitals can exert efforts individually or jointly to alleviate the negative impacts of undertreatment on patients, necessitating a balance between the benefits of delivering care and the associated costs. Using a game-theoretic model, we examine the strategic operations of hospitals to mitigate undertreatment in different effort exertion cases within a two-tier healthcare system. We find that without mitigation efforts, undertreatment could harm both the community and the city hospital when the treatment cost difference is significant, resulting in a lose-lose situation. One could expect that the community hospital has a greater motivation to mitigate its inherent undertreatment; however, our finding suggests that the city hospital may exert more mitigation effort, regardless of whether hospitals exert efforts individually or jointly. The result further illustrates that one hospital exerting mitigation effort individually consistently reaps benefits despite incurring effort costs, but possibly at the expense of the other hospital, leading to a win–lose situation. Finally, we demonstrate that the mitigation effort exerted by two hospitals jointly can convert a win–lose situation into a win–win situation when the loss caused by undertreatment is severe. Our management insights facilitate better decision-making on mitigating undertreatment in a two-tier healthcare system to promote effective utilization of medical resources.

Title: Spatial organization of multi-level services: A modeling framework for Hierarchical Districting
Authors: Giuseppe Bruno, Antonio Diglio, Andreana Ferraioli, Carmela Piccolo, Francisco Saldanha-da-Gama
Abstract: In this paper, novel, general and tractable optimization models are introduced for the spatial organization of multi-level services. Specifically, a hierarchically-structured districting plan is to be designed for geographical areas composed of multiple territorial units. This gives rise to a hierarchical districting problem. Different variants are analyzed accounting for features of practical relevance in real-world contexts, notably nestedness and coherency. The applicability of the proposed models is evidenced on small-to-mid-sized instances. Furthermore, the implications of incorporating multiple (often conflicting) planning criteria within different hierarchical structures are investigated. The results suggest that decision-makers may benefit from treating coherency as a “soft” requirement. This observation motivates the introduction of partial coherency, whereby a solution is deemed acceptable if it satisfies a prescribed minimum degree of coherency. The earlier formulations are accordingly extended to incorporate this concept, resulting in a unified model that subsumes the previous variants as special cases. Additional experiments demonstrate that partial coherency enables a flexible range of solutions that effectively address the inherent multi-criteria nature of hierarchical districting.

Title: Shared charging strategies at the electric bus depot: A robust optimization model
Authors: Di Huang, Zhou Jia, Zhitao Hu, Zhiyuan Liu, Ronghui Liu
Abstract: Reservation-based shared charging (R-SC) at bus depots leverages underutilized daytime charging capacity to support private electric vehicle (EV) users while generating additional revenue for bus operators and improving the overall utilization of electric buses (EBs) charging infrastructure. The key challenge, however, is managing the competing charging demands of private EVs without compromising charging reliability and operational needs of EBs. This study introduces a robust optimization modelling framework to schedule same-day EB charging while managing private EV charging demand, accounting for uncertainties in the EB power consumption. Two strategies are proposed to manage the demand of EV charging: a hard charging window with fixed pricing, and a soft charging window with variable, differentiated pricing. Numerical experiments demonstrate that R-SC significantly outperforms the first-come-first-served (FIFO) baseline in terms of economic performance and resource utilization. The soft charging window strategy, especially under high EV demand, enhances charging flexibility and increases the overall utilization of depot charging resources. Additionally, time-of-use pricing further strengthens the robustness of the proposed model. These findings have practical implications for managing shared charging facilities, and the modelling framework offers a valuable tool for designing resilient and efficient allocation strategies for shared charging.

Title: Technology selection for green transition using cap-and-trade in supply chains: A bilevel programming approach
Authors: Massimiliano Caramia, Anna Laura Pala, Giuseppe Stecca
Abstract: This paper investigates technology adoption for the decarbonization of supply chains under a cap-and-trade policy. A regulator sets a declining emissions cap over time and allocates a fixed budget across facilities, which then choose technology upgrades, production/procurement plans, and carbon trading to satisfy demand and comply with caps at minimum cost. We formulate the problem as a bilevel mixed-integer program combining plant-period caps, discrete monotone technology ladders, and facility budget dynamics with earmarked trading revenues. We propose three solution methods and compare them on extensive synthetic test beds. A steel supply chain case shows how transitional technologies and trading can accelerate the adoption of hydrogen-based routes and achieve the targeted emission abatement path. The results highlight when limited public funds are most effectively deployed and how trading complements intertemporal adoption.

Title: A data-driven robust optimization approach for omnichannel pricing, ordering, and blockchain adoption decisions under demand and perception uncertainties
Authors: Mingli Yuan, Ruozhen Qiu, Minghe Sun, Zhi-Ping Fan
Abstract: The integration of online and offline channels in omnichannel retailing enhances consumer convenience but also introduces challenges, including consumer perception uncertainty in online shopping and demand uncertainty across channels. Blockchain adoption in the online channel can mitigate consumer perception uncertainty by disclosing verified product information, thereby strengthening consumer trust. However, because blockchain adoption incurs additional costs, retailers must make a tradeoff between product information transparency and operational expense. This study develops a data-driven robust optimization approach to determine the optimal pricing, ordering, and blockchain activity level for an omnichannel retailer while ensuring service level requirements under demand uncertainty. Demand uncertainty is captured using data-driven uncertainty sets constructed using support vector clustering combined with kernel learning. Piecewise affine relaxation is applied to address nonlinearity in the model. A three-layer solution procedure is developed to solve the problem by selecting appropriate values for the adjustable and regularization parameters and ensuring the satisfaction of the service level requirements while maximizing profit. Numerical experiments are performed to assess the proposed model and demonstrate the efficacy of the three-layer solution procedure. Results demonstrate that blockchain adoption increases the robust profit from 1095,502.58 to 1116,004.28, indicating that blockchain can effectively enhance profitability, though excessive blockchain activity diminishes profit. The omnichannel retailer's optimal profits and decisions are influenced by factors such as the consumer valuation of online product information, information accuracy, and blockchain adoption cost. These findings offer actionable guidance for omnichannel retailers seeking to balance blockchain adoption costs with the benefits of improved product information transparency.

Title: Joint single and multi-trip delivery of consumable and non-consumable relief supplies with integrated deprivation costs
Authors: Jingwen Jiang, Kanglin Liu, Zhili Tian, Guangyu Zhu
Abstract: Disaster relief operations consistently grapple with significant challenges in response speed and resource allocation. A primary contributor to these difficulties is the distinct replenishment characteristics of non-consumable (e.g., tents) versus consumable (e.g., food) relief supplies. Conventional uniform distribution strategies often lead to resource mismatches when faced with these differing supply dynamics. This study addresses the critical facility location and allocation problems for both supply types by establishing a correspondence between supply consumption patterns and single/multi-trip delivery strategies. Our model's key findings reveal that the system may shift from optimizing delivery cadence and adjusting warehouse distribution to strengthening the pre-positioning intensity of existing warehouses as deprivation costs increase from a relatively moderate to a significantly higher rate. We propose a novel mixed-integer nonlinear programming model that integrates pre-disaster pre-positioning with post-disaster procurement. This model employs differentiated distribution strategies to more accurately quantify human suffering, while simultaneously balancing delivery and deprivation costs. To overcome the computational complexity posed by nonlinear deprivation cost functions, we develop efficient inner and outer approximation methods to linearize the model, significantly enhancing its computational efficiency. Notably, we establish a theoretical guarantee on the solution quality by deriving tight bounds on the maximum optimality gap of the inner and outer approximations. Extensive numerical experiments and real-world case studies demonstrate the model's certain applicability against the baseline model reported in this paper and offer a stable algorithmic performance improvement over the solver.

Title: New feasibility test driven adaptive large neighborhood search for time-dependent dial-a-ride problems
Authors: Wenjie Hu, Yang Wang, Jin-Kao Hao, Wei-Neng Chen, Jiliu Li, Xin Jin
Abstract: This work investigates three practical variants of the dial-a-ride problem with different objectives, called time-dependent dial-a-ride problems (TD-DARPs), where the travel time along each arc depends on the departure time of the vehicle from the starting node. We develop a general mathematical model to accommodate different objectives and attributes, and propose a feasibility test driven adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm based on the feature of time-dependent travel times. The algorithmic framework consists of three main modules: an adaptive destroy and repair procedure to enhance solution diversity, a tabu-based solution improvement method to refine solution quality, and a simulated annealing-based update criterion to escape local optima. Unlike the traditional and time-consuming feasibility test approach in the existing algorithms for TD-DARPs, our algorithm employs a novel feasibility test with linear time complexity, which leverages the first-in-first-out property and the structure of the travel time function to efficiently evaluate the feasibility of each insertion operation. Extensive numerical experiments on benchmark instances demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms the CPLEX solver and a state-of-the-art metaheuristic algorithm in terms of solution quality and running time.

Title: Sustainable food closed-loop supply chain resilience improvement problem
Authors: Ding Chen, Feng Chu, Ming Liu, Junkai He, Shijin Wang
Abstract: The transition to Industry 5.0 is reshaping supply chain management by emphasizing resilience, sustainability, and human-centricity. However, studies on food supply chains have not simultaneously examined returnable transport items and human-centricity under disruptions. To fill this gap, this paper examines a novel resilience improvement problem for the food closed-loop supply chain, considering two resilience strategies under disruptions. The objective is to minimize the total expected operational cost under worst-case scenarios. For the problem, we develop a distributionally robust chance-constrained programming model and, by exploiting its structural properties, derive an approximate mixed-integer linear programming reformulation. A real-world case study and experiments on randomly generated instances validate the robustness of the proposed strategies and solution approach. Key results demonstrate that resilience requires the synergy of the proposed temporary worker recruitment and returnable transport item inventory redundancy strategies, as isolated approaches are ineffective.

Title: Harmonizing sample average approximation and distributionally robust optimization
Authors: Ziliang Jin, Jianqiang Cheng, Daniel Zhuoyu Long, Kai Pan
Abstract: Decision-makers often encounter uncertainty, and the distribution of uncertain parameters plays a crucial role in making reliable decisions. However, complete information is rarely available. The sample average approximation (SAA) approach utilizes historical data to address this, but struggles with insufficient data. Conversely, moment-based distributionally robust optimization (DRO) effectively employs partial distributional information but can yield conservative solutions even with ample data. To bridge these approaches, we propose a novel method called harmonizing optimization (HO), which integrates SAA and DRO by adaptively adjusting the weights of data and information based on sample size N. This allows HO to amplify data effects in large samples while emphasizing information in smaller ones. More importantly, HO performs well across varying data sizes without needing to classify them as large or small. We provide practical methods for determining these weights and demonstrate that HO offers finite-sample performance guarantees and achieves asymptotic optimality. In addition, HO can be applied to enhance scenario reduction, improving approximation quality and reducing completion time by retaining critical information from reduced scenarios. Numerical results show significant advantages of HO in solution quality compared to Wasserstein-based DRO, and highlight its effectiveness in scenario reduction.

Title: Omni-channel retail inventory management with deep reinforcement learning
Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has gained increasing attention in inventory management, demonstrating strong potential compared to traditional heuristic approaches. However, most existing studies rely on simulations under idealized assumptions of known and stationary demand distributions—conditions that rarely hold in practice. This study investigates the effectiveness of DRL in real-world omnichannel store-level inventory management, where demand is unknown, time-varying, correlated with external factors, and managed across a large number of Stock Keeping Units (SKUs). To address the resulting scale and heterogeneity, we propose a Mixture-of-Experts Proximal Policy Optimization (MOE-PPO) framework that integrates multiple specialized expert networks through a dynamic gating mechanism, enhancing scalability and robustness. Using real retail data, we conduct extensive experiments that compare the proposed DRL framework with practical industry benchmarks across various scenarios, including limited data availability and diverse demand characteristics. Empirical results show that MOE-PPO consistently outperforms both traditional heuristics and standard PPO, yielding significant improvements in inventory performance. The findings offer actionable insights into the practical application of DRL in dynamic, uncertain retail environments and demonstrate its potential to enhance decision-making, operational efficiency, and overall supply chain performance.

Title: An exact solution approach for the multi-period EV home health care routing and scheduling problem with uncertain travel times and service durations
Authors: Yunqiang Yin, Xiaochang Liu, Ling Qing, Huaxin Qiu, Xiaowen Wei
Abstract: The home health care routing and scheduling problem (HHCRSP) has attracted increasing attention from the medical operations management community. Given the pervasive uncertainties in travel times and service durations inherent to home health care scheduling and vehicle routing, we study the HHCRSP with electric vehicles (EVs), which involves using EVs to transport caregivers serving patients with time-constrained appointments across a multi-period planning horizon. This problem incorporates inherent characteristics including the continuity-of-service requirement, diagnosis and treatment regulation, and hierarchical service strategy. We cast the problem into a robust optimization model to minimize the total operational costs, composed of caregiver-assignment costs, travel costs, and incompatibility penalty costs, where budget-based robust sets are used to mitigate the uncertainties in travel times and service durations. To solve the robust optimization model exactly, we develop a customized logic Benders decomposition algorithm, in which a dynamic programming-based labeling algorithm is designed to solve the Benders sub-problems. A three-stage heuristic strategy is proposed to generate preliminary feasible solutions to tighten the initial lower bound of the relaxed Benders master problem, and a binary variable elimination strategy is introduced to reduce the number of binary variables of the Benders master problem. Extensive numerical studies are then conducted to verify the effectiveness of the binary variable reduction and warm start strategies, qualify the performance of the developed algorithm, and ascertain the benefits of accounting for uncertainty as well as the robustness of the model.

Title: E-commerce platform information sharing and product quality positioning competition
Authors: Qian Chen, Ju Zhao, Jingxian Chen
Abstract: A new business model of e-commerce platforms empowering brand owners with product innovation through information sharing is emerging. The sharing of consumer preference information can help brands accurately target the quality positioning of new products, while also changing competition intensity of substitutive products. This paper examines the strategic interaction between e-platform information sharing and the quality positioning of competing brands. By studying the conditions under which a strategy yields higher profits, we find that when the quality positioning is exogenous, the e-platform's information sharing strategy depends on the product quality differential among brand owners and the consumer's sensitivity to quality. However, when the quality positioning is endogenous, the e-platform's strategic choice requires a trade-off between consumer quality sensitivity and the intensity of competition between brand owners. This distinction yields interesting findings absent in the existing literature: when the quality is exogenous, the e-platform must abandon the presumption that “mitigating competition necessarily enhances profitability”. Conversely, when the quality is endogenous, the e-platform should actively promote quality differentiation as a means to alleviate competitive pressure. In addition, the problem is extended to the scenario of asymmetric brands with different market sizes. It is found that the larger the market size gap, the more the e-platform will use the information gap advantage to help brands differentiate their positioning. We also examine the robustness of these findings in several cases of extensions of our model.

Title: Design of alliance-based coordination mechanisms for renal relief
Authors: Sırma Karakaya, Burcu Balcik, Evrim D. Gunes
Abstract: Disasters often render hemodialysis clinics inoperable, posing severe risks to patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), who depend on regular dialysis for survival. When services are disrupted, patients must be transferred rapidly to operational clinics. Establishing a coordination mechanism before a disaster can support timely matching of patients to available clinics and reduce post-disaster chaos. We introduce the Alliance Network Design Problem, which proactively forms alliances among clinics to support coordinated renal relief. These alliances enable resource pooling and pre-assignment of backup clinics to patients. We formulate the ANDP as a two-stage stochastic mixed integer programming model that determines alliance relationships and backup clinic assignments under uncertainty in post-disaster clinic capacities. To address computational challenges, we propose a Hybrid-Sample Average Approximation (H-SAA) method integrating Latin Hypercube Sampling and Importance Sampling. We show that H-SAA outperforms conventional SAA approaches, particularly by better capturing low-probability, high-impact scenarios. A case study of the hemodialysis network in Istanbul, Türkiye, demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach in strengthening disaster preparedness for ESKD patients. Our results show that alliance formation mitigates the adverse effects of disasters on dialysis continuity relative to a no-alliance setting. We also provide policy-relevant insights by evaluating complementary resilience strategies, including region-specific clinic fortification and post-disaster capacity augmentation.

Title: Manufacturer’s proactive strategy from the perspective of risk-aversion: A novel two-stage integrated model
Authors: Haidong Yang, Quanchu Lao, Biyu Liu, Yingming Wang
Abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage integrated model to compare the effectiveness of proactive strategies (PSs) for mitigating supply chain disruptions from a risk-averse perspective. First, factors influencing the effectiveness of PSs are analyzed, with supply and demand uncertainties characterized using a scenario-based method and a Markov chain model, respectively. Second, a novel two-stage integrated model is developed, which aims to minimize the expected worst-case costs through the Conditional Value-at-Risk approach. Finally, the model is validated through numerical examples, including comparison and sensitivity analyses to assess the effectiveness of single and combination of PSs in addressing potential disruption risks. The results indicate that: (1) the performance of PSs, or their combinations, varies according to the manufacturer's level of risk-aversion. At high levels of risk-aversion, the benefits of combined PSs become increasingly significant; (2) the effectiveness of combined strategies is not always superior to that of single-PS. Indeed, a strategy that generally performs poorly can contribute to an effective combination, and vice versa, due to interactions among different strategies; and (3) the effectiveness of PSs is influenced by several factors, with risk-aversion, demand state transition, and pre-disruption budget being critical determinants. This study provides valuable insights for manufacturers’ supply chain risk management.

Title: On the impact of operation flexibility in the flexible job-shop scheduling problem
Abstract: Due to its complexity and practical interest, the flexible job-shop scheduling problem has become one of the most studied scheduling problems. However, to our knowledge, all studies assume that the flexibility of operations (the possibility for an operation to be assigned to a machine from a given set of machines) is given when solving the problem. In this paper, we analyze the impact of operation flexibility when minimizing the makespan, with a particular focus on optimizing qualification decisions. Qualifying a machine for an operation means making the machine eligible to perform the operation. Only a limited number of non-eligible machines can be qualified, i.e. are qualifiable, for an operation. A bi-objective scheduling problem is introduced, where both the makespan and the qualification cost are minimized. A mathematical model is proposed, and new problem instances are generated to support several analyses. First, the impact of operation flexibility on the makespan is studied. Second, the level of flexibility required to achieve a given makespan is investigated. Third, the trade-off between the makespan and the qualification cost is mapped, and situations in which qualifications are fixed are compared with situations in which qualifications are optimized jointly with scheduling. The numerical results show that determining a limited but well-chosen set of qualifications substantially reduces the makespan, and that jointly optimizing qualification decisions with scheduling reaches the same performance with significantly fewer qualifications than when all qualifiable machines are qualified. Various managerial insights are presented. In particular, the level of operation flexibility available in a flexible job shop has more impact on performance than the choice of the scheduling algorithm. Some limitations of the study and related perspectives are also discussed.

Title: The impact of subsidies on wind farms under uncertainty: A real options approach
Authors: Xinyu Wang, Xinya Liu, Shuhua Zhang
Abstract: Renewable energy has grown rapidly, increasing market uncertainty and investment risks. To mitigate these risks and encourage investment incentives, governments have implemented various subsidy schemes to support wind farm development. This paper investigates the influence of three distinct subsidies (fixed price, fixed premium, and minimum price guarantee policies) on the investment timing, optimal capacity decisions, and social welfare under uncertainty. When making investment decisions, sponsors consider both endogenous credit and merchant risks. We model sponsors’ decisions as an optimal stopping problem. Using a real options approach, the cut-off electricity price and payoff functions are derived under each subsidy scheme. In particular, we divide the subsidy into three levels in the minimum price guarantee subsidy scheme. At the moderate level, a critical subsidy threshold, which effectively distinguishes the impact of subsidy on default risk, is found. Next, we analyze the intricate interaction between operational decisions to expand production capacity and financial decisions to default on Special Purpose Vehicles, resulting in diverse capacity expansion strategies. Our findings show that fixed premium and minimum price guarantee policies effectively alleviate underinvestment caused by inefficiency, and we further identify the optimal subsidy levels. Lastly, we apply the theoretical model to study China Datang New Energy and provide useful managerial insights.

Title: A two-stage stochastic programming approach for strategic rolling stock scheduling in passenger railway transport
Authors: Siqiao Li, Rolf van Lieshout, Patrick Stokkink
Abstract: Conventional railway planning follows a sequential approach in which rolling stock scheduling is performed only after timetables are constructed, forcing early-stage line-planning decisions to rely on simplified rolling stock cost approximations. The lack of precise cost information hampers line-plan evaluation and limits the design of cost-efficient services. This study considers rolling stock scheduling in a strategic setting, aiming to estimate fleet size and operational costs for a given line plan without solving the timetabling problem. Since predefined train services are unavailable at this level, unlike in tactical planning, we introduce a network representation incorporating shunting movements like coupling and uncoupling. To account for demand uncertainty, a two-stage stochastic programming approach is proposed, in which first-stage decisions determine fleet acquisition and second-stage decisions optimize rolling stock circulation, including shunting, under each demand scenario. Two models are developed, differing in whether the fleet size is estimated using a flow-based or circulation-based approach. The applicability of the proposed models is demonstrated using instances derived from the Dutch Intercity network. Compared to a trip-based benchmark, the circulation-based model yields more accurate cost estimates, while short and simple cycles retain most of its value at much lower computational cost. Moreover, stochastic planning better captures the procurement–service trade-off under demand uncertainty and produces more robust fleet plans than a deterministic approach. Under strong emphasis on investment costs, fleet choices are dominated by flexible, cost-effective unit types. Allowing shunting enables flexible capacity redistribution, reducing fleet requirements and investment costs while maintaining comparable service levels.

Title: A predict-then-optimize framework for exposure allocation in online-to-offline platforms under uncertainty
Authors: Yani Ji, Nan Yang, Ran Ao, Yanting Jin, Yuxin Hong, Zhu Meng, Jie Chen, Yun Long, Ning Zhu
Abstract: While online-to-offline (O2O) platforms have reshaped how consumers discover and choose among local services, they encounter a significant challenge in ensuring that recommended content effectively translates into user engagement. In this study, we propose a predict-then-optimize framework for category-level exposure proportion optimization. Specifically, we develop a pooling-and-boosting (PAB) method that leverages hierarchical and distance exposure features to predict click-through volume, and then incorporate the predicted outcomes into the exposure allocation decision while accounting for practical operational constraints. To characterize uncertainty in hierarchical and distance exposure distributions, we construct a scenario-wise Wasserstein ambiguity set and propose a distributionally robust chance-constrained problem (DRCCP) that can be reformulated as a tractable mixed-integer linear program (MILP). We validate the proposed framework using real-world data from a major O2O platform. The results show that the PAB method achieves lower out-of-sample prediction errors than benchmark methods, and hierarchical exposure is the most critical feature affecting click-through volume. Furthermore, the Wasserstein DRCCP model achieves more reliable tail-risk performance out of sample, and the numerical results provide valuable managerial insights for O2O platform operators.

Title: Dynamic pricing of targeted coupons in competitive online auction platforms
Abstract: Targeted coupons are an increasingly central feature of the competitive dynamics among online auction platforms. However, the combined impact of competition and dynamic pricing on these couponing strategies is not yet fully understood. In this study, we model two auction platforms that enter the market sequentially to sell substitutable items to bidders with heterogeneous valuations and participation costs. We develop a game-theoretic model to analyze the equilibrium outcomes of targeted coupon strategies under both commitment and dynamic pricing, examining the effects of competition and pricing flexibility. Our analysis reveals a novel competition effect that extends related results in the literature: under dynamic pricing, competition can surprisingly increase the early entrant's profit. We also show that competition and dynamic pricing jointly create a greater incentive for platforms to use targeted coupons, while dynamic pricing itself moderates the impact of competition. Moreover, our main results are largely robust to extensions considering imperfect customer targeting capabilities, low-valuation bidder loyalty, and the endogeneity of high-valuation bidders.

Title: An economic analysis of eligibility thresholds for ad-revenue-sharing programs on content platforms
Authors: Ruomeng Hu, Haiyang Feng, Nan Feng, Minqiang Li
Abstract: Content platforms often implement ad-revenue-sharing programs, displaying advertisements alongside eligible creators’ content and sharing the resulting revenue with them. Eligibility for these programs is typically determined by follower count thresholds, which platforms adjust in response to market dynamics. This study develops an analytical model to examine how different market characteristics influence the platform's optimal eligibility threshold, user engagement, creators’ earnings, and the platform's profit. We find that an increase in ad-free basic revenue leads the platform to raise the eligibility threshold when creator competition is intense, whereas reducing the threshold is optimal under weaker competition. When advertisements significantly disrupt user experience or when eligible creators exert strong competitive pressure, stronger cross-side network effects or weaker creator competition induce the platform to tighten eligibility. Interestingly, under certain conditions, lower ad-free basic revenue or higher content production cost can benefit both the platform and ad-supported creators. The study also extends the model to incorporate asymmetric cross-side network effects, heterogeneous content production costs, and platform competition, demonstrating the robustness of our main findings.

Title: Exact solutions to the two-dimensional bin packing problem with due dates
Authors: Milad Dehghan, Sergey Polyakovskiy, Rym M’Hallah
Abstract: The two-dimensional non-oriented bin packing problem with due dates packs a set of rectangular items that can be rotated by 90 o into identical rectangular bins. The bins, which act as batches, have equal processing times. An item’s lateness is the difference between its completion time and its due date, where an item has the completion time of its assigned bin. The problem searches for a feasible solution that minimizes the maximum lateness. This mini-max problem is computationally challenging: Its solution space is very large with many symmetrical packing layouts. Herein, we propose two types of exact methods to solve the problem: three mixed-integer programs (MIPs), strengthened with a set of feasibility and symmetry-breaking constraints, and a constraint program (CP) that takes advantage of the strength of the CP-specific two-dimensional non-overlap constraint and the cumulative scheduling relaxations of the packing problem. Our most successful proposed MIP solves 50% of the benchmark instances, with 20 to 60 items. Our CP solves 66% of the benchmark instances including large instances with 100 items. It further reduces the 14% optimality gap of benchmark instances to 8%. On benchmark real-life industrial instances, which are mostly very large-sized, our CP suggests that existing primal and dual gaps can be further tightened.

Title: Pivot-Linked Elicitation: A unified approach to hierarchical weight elicitation and its application to best–worst methods
Abstract: We study weight elicitation in Multiple Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) when decision criteria are organized hierarchically. We show that the conventional practice of eliciting weights separately at each level can lead to practical and conceptual limitations, including reliance on abstract upper-level judgments and the fragmentation of consistency across independent sub-models. To address these issues, we propose the PIvot-Linked Elicitation (PILE) framework, which links groups through a small set of pivot criteria and integrates intra- and inter-group preference information into a single model. We instantiate PILE for best–worst methods, deriving nonlinear and linear PILE–Best-Worst Method (BWM) formulations, and illustrate the approach on two published use cases. The results demonstrate how PILE preserves the cognitive benefits of hierarchical structuring while enabling a more holistic and consistency-aware elicitation.

Title: Probabilistic selling with pity time mechanisms: Optimal pricing and consumer welfare
Authors: Yung-Hsun Chang, Chia-Wei Kuo, Kwei-Long Huang
Abstract: Probabilistic selling is a popular strategy used by companies to segment markets and boost profits, but its increasing adoption has raised consumer concerns, particularly regarding concealed probability information and associations with gambling. To address these issues, many sellers disclose details about the probabilities of their products, and some implement a “pity time” mechanism, which guarantees that if a consumer fails to obtain her desired product after a specified number of attempts, the seller will deliver it directly. This study examines the adoption of pity time mechanisms in probabilistic selling with vertically differentiated products and diverse consumer types. The findings show that when only a probabilistic product is offered, the pity time mechanism increases the seller's profit and improves consumer and social welfare, especially when quality differences between products are small or moderate, or when fewer consumers demand high-quality products. For sellers offering multiple products, the mechanism is more profitable when quality differences are small to moderate, or when more consumers prefer high-quality products. Moreover, whether the seller offers only a probabilistic product or multiple types of products, implementing a pity time mechanism consistently benefits the seller, consumers, and society, achieving a win-win-win outcome to the stakeholders.

Title: Enhancing supply chain network resilience against disruption risks: Event-wise robust optimization with accelerated benders decomposition
Authors: Qin Huang, Laijun Zhao, Changzhi Wu
Abstract: Supply chain networks are increasingly susceptible to unforeseen disruptions, leading to hub facility failures, volatile customer demand, and impaired transportation performance. To address these challenges, this study proposes a robust two-stage approach to enhance the resilience of a supply chain network against disruption risks. Our approach introduces a event-wise ambiguity set to describe uncertainties in hub capacity losses and customer demand fluctuations. Two distributionally robust optimization models are developed under assumptions of independence and correlation, respectively, and are reformulated into tractable mixed-integer programming models. In addition, the framework incorporates resource reallocation, outsourcing, and lost sales strategies to enhance both resilience and cost-effectiveness within the two stage logistics network. To efficiently solve large-scale instances, an accelerated Benders decomposition algorithm incorporating advanced acceleration techniques is proposed. Extensive numerical experiments validate the proposed approach, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating disruption risks, enhancing supply chain resilience, and improving service levels. This study contributes novel theoretical insights and offers actionable guidelines for emergency response and resilient network design in uncertain supply chain environments, thereby equipping decision-makers with robust strategies to enhance system performance under uncertainty.

Title: A new churn prediction framework incorporating spatio-temporal information for the retail industry
Authors: Bing Zhu, Yuanyuan Li, Tao Gu, Cheng Qian, Seppe vanden Broucke
Abstract: Customer churn prediction plays a vital role in the retail industry's marketing practice. With the advancement of mobile Internet and location-aware devices, retail companies are now equipped with vast customer behavioral data, including spatio-temporal information. However, fully leveraging spatio-temporal information in churn prediction is complex and challenging. In this study, we propose a new churn prediction framework for the retail sector, effectively integrating spatio-temporal information of customer behavior. The framework introduces new feature extraction methods that generate spatial, temporal, and semantic features based on customer events. These features are then fused with behavioral features using deep learning techniques. Extensive empirical experiments using real-world retail datasets show that the proposed approach significantly outperforms other benchmark methods. We also conduct a comprehensive analysis of the influence of different extracted features to provide valuable insights.

Title: Scheduling for peak load management over time
Authors: Myungho Lee, Kangbok Lee, Michael Pinedo
Abstract: This paper studies a scheduling approach that reduces catastrophic-disaster damage by allocating tasks to intervals within a given time horizon, based on task importance. We model the problem as a non-preemptive single-machine cyclic scheduling problem that minimizes the peak interval load, where each interval load is defined as the total weight of jobs being processed within a time interval. We analyze the problem under three different parameter settings: the length of the interval, the number of distinct weights, and the number of distinct processing times. We determine the computational complexity for a variety of problem settings and develop approximation algorithms for NP-hard problems. For some of these problems, we also derive inapproximability ratios. In addition, we develop practical algorithms that select the better solution obtained from approximation and greedy algorithms, and demonstrate their effectiveness on randomly generated instances.

Title: Herd or heard? Disentangling social influence and personal taste in music listening with a probabilistic topic model
Authors: Hongyi Zha, Jiapeng Liu, Miłosz Kadziński, Jinnan Huang, Xiuwu Liao
Abstract: In large-scale music platforms, choices reflect both individual preferences and popularity trends. Understanding the interplay between these forces is a core challenge for developing an interpretable listening prediction framework. We propose the Probabilistic Disentanglement Model (PDM), which, for each play, determines whether the choice is interest- or popularity-driven. Our model characterizes users’ general preferences using a mixture of latent interests while concurrently modeling herd behavior by treating track popularity as a generative factor. A sparsity-inducing prior is incorporated to effectively disentangle these two components within a user's listening history. For speed and scale, we use coordinate-ascent variational inference, which enables practical training on large datasets. On the Last.fm “30Music” dataset, PDM shows statistically significant gains in predictive accuracy over strong baselines based on matrix factorization, topic modeling, and neural collaborative filtering. Results are stable across different numbers of topics, and ablations show that removing latent popularity or the user/experience module reduces accuracy. The method is highly interpretable, yielding user herding scores, user interest mixtures, and item popularity estimates. They help understand listening behavior and manage popularity effects. In summary, PDM offers a straightforward, scalable, and interpretable approach to separating taste from popularity, thereby enhancing prediction and delivering valuable insights for auditing and control.

Title: How does digital transformation influence trade credit in manufacturing firms? A signaling theory perspective
Authors: Lishuang Jia, Jiaqi Tian, Jianhu Cai, Wenlian Gao, Xiaoqing Hu
Abstract: The widespread diffusion of digital technologies has fundamentally reshaped the operational and financial environments of manufacturing firms, yet how digital transformation (DT) affects trade credit remains theoretically ambiguous and empirically inconclusive. Using panel data on Chinese manufacturing firms from 2007 to 2023, this study estimates fixed-effects models to examine the relationship between DT and trade credit and to test the moderating roles of analyst attention and ownership concentration from a signaling theory perspective. The findings indicate a U-shaped relationship between DT and trade credit and show that analyst attention and ownership concentration moderate this relationship. Further heterogeneity analyses indicate that this nonlinear pattern varies across firms with different levels of executive digital expertise, R& D intensity, and supplier concentration. We additionally employ two-stage least squares and a difference-in-differences design to mitigate potential endogeneity concerns, and a series of robustness checks confirm the stability of our results. This study reconciles conflicting findings in the prior literature by identifying a U-shaped relationship between DT and trade credit, thereby advancing the theoretical understanding of DT as a complex signal in supply chain finance and offering practical guidance for manufacturing firms seeking to strategically align DT with trade credit management.

Title: Strategic adoption of blended treatment modes in a competitive healthcare market: Single-hospital or cross-hospital
Authors: Yufei Ge, Gaoji Sun, Yanfei Lan
Abstract: Telemedicine has emerged as a strategic complement to traditional in-person care, offering enhanced continuity and effectiveness through blended treatment that integrates online and offline visits to support continuous care. We examine two distinct delivery modes for blended treatment, namely the single-hospital and cross-hospital modes, in an asymmetric competition setting involving a telemedicine-capable hospital and a traditional hospital. Specifically, in the single-hospital mode, the telemedicine-capable hospital delivers both online and offline care components internally. In the cross-hospital mode, the telemedicine-capable hospital provides the online component, while either hospital can deliver the offline component. Utilizing a game-theoretic framework, we examine the strategic adoption of these two modes by the telemedicine-capable hospital and analyze the resulting competitive and operational implications. Surprisingly, we find that a telemedicine-capable hospital may suffer losses from launching blended treatment, as the gains from market expansion are outweighed by intensified competition and internal cannibalization, resulting in lower profits. Furthermore, even when blended treatment is profitable, the telemedicine-capable hospital may still prefer the single-hospital mode over the cross-hospital mode under certain conditions, even at the expense of its rival's profits, while consistently improving both patient and social welfare. By contrast, adopting the cross-hospital mode can yield a triple–win outcome for the telemedicine-capable hospital, its rival, and patients, and also enhance social welfare. This study advances theoretical understanding of healthcare system dynamics and provides strategic recommendations for healthcare organizations navigating digital transformation.

Title: Dynamic physician scheduling in emergency departments among different rooms with uncertain patient arrivals
Authors: Ding Jin, Chengkai Wang, Ran Liu
Abstract: In emergency departments (EDs), patients are classified into different severity levels and directed to either the resuscitation room or general consultation rooms. Given limited physician resources, managers usually dynamically allocate physicians between these rooms to meet fluctuating patient demand. This real-time allocation and scheduling is challenging due to the uncertainties in patient arrivals and treatment durations. Motivated by the operational challenges of our partner ED, we investigate this dynamic physician scheduling problem between resuscitation and general consultation rooms. We model the patient flow as a time-varying parallel queueing system and formulate the physician allocation problem as a Markov decision process. A bidirectional iterative algorithm is developed to solve the Markov decision process using predicted patient arrivals. To improve real-time adaptability, we propose an online policy update method that integrates linear regression with online learning to predict arrivals during the decision horizon. The physician allocation policy is then updated using these real-time predictions. Numerical experiments using real hospital data show that our methods outperform classical scheduling rules and current hospital practices.
